newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Iridium World in IPO and satellite race.
newsitem.headline: Iridium World in IPO and satellite race.

text.p: Iridium World Communications, having priced a US$240 million initial public offering this week, expects to keep its 1998 deadline for launching its satellite service, a senior official said on Tuesday.

"It was a prime time to be rounding up our equity financing, an excellent time for an IPO," said Robert Kinzie, chairman of Iridium LLC, an international consortium of telecommunication companies established to operate the Iridium satellite network.
The global telephone service via 66 low-orbit satellites, a network estimated to cost US$3.4 billion, will be ready to run at the end of next year.
Proceeds from the IPO will be used by Iridium World for development of the satellite project and corporate purposes.
The 12 million shares of class A common stock were priced at US$20 each.

Kinzie said the global satellite project was on schedule and more progress had been made in international regulatory markets with countries agreeing to open markets to competition for network operators and service providers.
Iridium has launched five satellites and is in the lead to start a global satellite network for hand-held phones, pagers, internet and facsimile services.
Competitor Globalstar Telecommunications Ltd will send a satellite into space during the third quarter of this year and aims to launch a US$2.5 billion satellite system by early 1999.
